mainTopic: חזקה in a field of trees, splitting trees and land between two holders, and keeping trees when selling land
overview: The גמרא first uses רבי ישמעאל's rule, that one kind of fruit counts as חזקה for all the fruit, to explain why eating from different groups of trees in different years still counts as חזקה for the whole field. It then limits that rule in two ways. The skipped trees must have had no fruit that year, and the trees must be spread throughout the field. Next comes a case where one person held the trees and another held the land. רב זביד says each owns what he held. רב פפא objects that the land owner could then force the trees out, so he rules that the tree owner gets the trees plus half the land. Finally, the גמרא says that someone who sells land but keeps the trees still owns land for them, even according to רבי עקיבא. It explains that רבי עקיבא's 'generous seller' rule was said about a pit or cistern, which does not weaken the land, and it begins to explain how trees are different. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's rule explains why groups of trees support each other
steps.stepSummary: Just as רבי ישמעאל says one kind of fruit counts as חזקה for all the fruit in a field, eating from one group of trees counts as חזקה for the other groups too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי ישמעאל say that one kind of fruit counts as חזקה for all the fruits? Here too, these trees count as חזקה for those, and those count as חזקה for these.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why eating fruit from different groups of trees in different years can still be a full חזקה. It does this by comparing it to a rule of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that harvesting one kind of produce is enough to show ownership of the whole field. The גמרא applies the same idea here: each year's eating from one group of trees shows ownership of all the trees. So the separate groups join together into one complete חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumed ownership, built by using a property like an owner over time
One kind of fruit or produce
Here too; the same logic applies in this case

phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yishmael say:
one kind of fruit is a presumption of ownership
for all the fruits?
phrases.notes: He means all the produce in the whole field.

phrases.english: Here too,
these trees are a presumption of ownership for those,
and those trees are a presumption of ownership for these.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of a field where fruit was eaten from different groups of trees in different years.
steps.raayaObject: That eating from some trees each year counts as חזקה for the whole field.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל's rule that one kind of fruit counts as חזקה for all the fruits.

steps.title: First limit: only when the other trees did not produce
steps.stepSummary: The rule works only if the trees he skipped gave no fruit that year. If they gave fruit and he did not eat it, there is no חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only where the other trees did not produce fruit. But if they produced and he did not eat, it is not a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a first limit to the rule it just explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skipping trees that had no fruit is normal and shows nothing. But if the other trees had fruit and he left it alone, he did not act like an owner of those trees. So that year's eating does not count for them.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only (introduces a limit)

phrases.english: And this statement applies
where the other trees did not produce fruit,
but if they produced and he did not eat,
it is not a presumption of ownership.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The groups of trees support each other only when the skipped trees had no fruit; if they had fruit and he did not eat it, there is no חזקה.

steps.title: Second limit: the trees must be scattered through the field
steps.stepSummary: The rule works only if the trees are spread out across the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only when the trees are scattered about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit to the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trees are spread over the whole field, eating from them shows ownership of the whole field. If they are bunched in one area, he only shows ownership of that area.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when (introduces a condition)

steps.whatToRemember: Eating from different groups of trees in different years counts as חזקה for the whole field, but only if (1) the skipped trees had no fruit, and (2) the trees are spread out across the field.

phrases.english: And this is only when the trees are scattered about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the rule from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The trees count for the whole field only when they are spread throughout it.

steps.title: רב זביד: one owns the trees, the other owns the land
steps.stepSummary: If one person held the trees and another held the land, רב זביד rules that each acquired what he held.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this one took possession of the trees and that one took possession of the land, רב זביד says: this one acquired the trees and that one acquired the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case about a field with trees, where two different people each held a different part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד gives the simple answer: each person gets only what he held. The tree holder gets the trees and the land holder gets the land. This sets up רב פפא's objection.

phrases.english: If this one took possession of the trees,
and that one took possession of the land,
Rav Zevid says:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה קָנָה אִילָנוֹת, וְזֶה קָנָה קַרְקַע.
phrases.english: This one acquired the trees, and that one acquired the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הֶחְזִיק בָּאִילָנוֹת וְזֶה הֶחְזִיק בַּקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case, still about חזקה in a field with trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person acquires only what he held: one the trees, the other the land.

steps.title: רב פפא: then the land owner could force the trees out
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects that by רב זביד's ruling, the tree owner has no land at all, so the land owner could tell him to dig up his trees and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: If so, the tree owner has nothing in the land. Then the land owner could say to him: Uproot your trees, take them, and go!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב זביד's ruling by showing where it leads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tree owner owns no land, his trees have no right to stand there. The land owner could simply order him to remove them. That result makes the tree owner's חזקה worthless, so רב זביד's ruling cannot be right.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, אֵין לוֹ לְבַעַל אִילָנוֹת
phrases.english: If so, the owner of the trees has nothing
in the land at all;

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא לֵיהּ בַּעַל קַרְקַע לְבַעַל אִילָנוֹת:
phrases.english: let the owner of the land say to the owner of the trees:
Uproot your trees, take them, and go!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב זביד's ruling in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's ruling that the tree holder gets only the trees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shows the ruling leads to an unacceptable result: the land owner could force the tree owner to remove his trees.

steps.title: רב פפא's ruling: the tree owner also gets half the land
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules instead that the tree holder gets the trees plus half the land, and the land holder gets the other half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: This one acquired the trees and half the land, and that one acquired half the land.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב זביד's view, רב פפא gives his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tree owner now gets a share of the land, so he cannot be forced to remove his trees. The land is split in half between the two. This fixes the problem raised in step 5.
steps.whatToRemember: By רב פפא: the one who held the trees gets the trees plus half the land; the one who held the land gets the other half.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
This one acquired the trees and half the land,
and that one acquired half the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב זביד's ruling after the objection in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each person gets only what he held (רב זביד).
steps.terutzMaskana: The tree holder gets the trees and half the land, so his trees cannot be forced out.

steps.title: Selling land but keeping the trees: he keeps land too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that someone who sells land but keeps the trees for himself still owns land for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he sold land and kept the trees for himself, he has land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related case and says its ruling is obvious. This sets up the next step, which explains why it holds even by רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a seller holds back trees, he holds back the land they need too. The גמרא calls this obvious, but it still needs to show that רבי עקיבא would agree.

keyTerms.meaning: He kept back, held for himself

phrases.english: It is obvious:
if he sold land and kept the trees for himself,
he has land.
phrases.notes: He means the land around and under the trees he kept.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא מָכַר קַרְקַע וְשִׁיֵּיר אִילָנוֹת לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from חזקה to a related sale case about trees and land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sells land but keeps the trees still owns land for the trees.

steps.title: Even רבי עקיבא agrees: his rule is about a pit or cistern
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי עקיבא, who says a seller sells generously, would agree here, because his rule was said about a pit or cistern. The next step continues this sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי עקיבא, who says a seller sells generously, that was said about a pit or a cistern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא heads off a possible question: doesn't רבי עקיבא say a seller gives everything? It answers that his rule was about a pit or cistern. The next step explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a seller sells generously, so when he keeps a pit or cistern he does not keep land around it. The גמרא limits that rule to pits and cisterns. The next step starts to explain why trees are different.
steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. The next step explains why a pit or cistern is different from trees.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Akiva, who says:
a seller sells generously,
that applies concerning a pit or a cistern,
phrases.notes: That's the case of רבי עקיבא, where the seller keeps the pit or cistern but no land around it, not even a path to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר מוֹכֵר בְּעַיִן יָפָה מוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains that the ruling of step 7 holds even according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's rule that a seller sells generously was said about a pit or cistern, so it does not decide the case of trees.

steps.title: A pit or cistern does not weaken the land, but trees are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא's rule fits a pit or cistern: they do not weaken the land. It then starts to say that trees are a different story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they (the pit and cistern) do not weaken the land. But trees...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind the distinction it started in step 8, and then opens a contrast with trees. This line sets up the next move, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the גמרא said רבי עקיבא's 'generous seller' rule was said about a pit or cistern. Now it explains why: a pit or cistern does not weaken the land around it. The word אֲבָל ('but') signals that trees will be treated differently, and the explanation of that difference comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling about trees yet. It only gives the reason for the pit and cistern case and begins the contrast. The ruling about trees finishes on the next amud.

phrases.english: since they do not weaken the land;
but trees,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning begun in step 8 by explaining why רבי עקיבא's rule fits a pit or cistern, and opens a contrast with trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pit or cistern does not weaken the land, which is why רבי עקיבא's rule applies to them. Trees are about to be treated differently.
